Two people editing the same object

Case by case, what SATOM does when two people, two tabs, or a person and a job change the same object or the same row of an object — who is blocked, who wins, what each one sees, what reaches the device and what is written to the Audit Log.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsprotection.edit network.edit
📍 WhereObject editor, Server Policy page, the dialogs of every product's GUI-layout pages, and every job that writes to a device

What is it?#

This article answers one question in detail: what happens when two people (or one person in two tabs, or a person and a job) change the same object, or the same row of an object, on the same device? It covers every case SATOM handles, plus the cases it deliberately does not.

SATOM uses two mechanisms that work together:

  1. The edit lock (Edit locks) decides who may write while someone has the object open. It is checked by every writer, not only the editors.
  2. The stale-value check decides whether a save is based on what the device holds now. It catches changes the lock cannot see: changes made before you opened the page, and changes made on the device itself.

ℹ️Note

New in 4.11.0. On 4.10.1 and earlier only the object editor checked the lock, a lock belonged to a user rather than a page, and the last save won without a warning.

The two mechanisms in numbers#

Edit lock Stale-value check
Taken / done when An existing object is opened for editing Every save from an editor
Belongs to One page load (a browser tab) of one user One save
Lifetime Renewed every 30 s while the page is open; expires 120 s after the last renewal The save itself
Checked against Every PUT, PATCH and DELETE that targets the object or one of its rows A fresh read of the object (or row) from the device, just before the write
On refusal HTTP 409, nothing is sent to the device HTTP 409, nothing is sent to the device
Audit Log config.write.edit_locked (writes from jobs and other non-editor paths) config.update.overwrote when you choose to overwrite

Case by case: two people, the same object#

Alice opens the object first; Bob opens it afterwards.

# Case What Bob sees What reaches the device
1 Bob opens the object Banner 🔒 Being edited by alice. Saving is blocked to avoid a conflict. with Take over. Save answers This object is locked by another user. Take over the lock first. Nothing
2 Bob's save reaches the server anyway (a page opened earlier, the API) "pol-shop" is being edited by alice. Take over the edit lock first; nothing was sent to the device. Nothing
3 Bob presses Take over The banner disappears; Bob can save Bob's save, when he makes it
4 …and Alice then saves Alice's page shows ⚠ Your edit lock was lost (expired or taken). Reload before saving. at its next renewal; a save she sends is refused like case 2 Nothing from Alice
5 Alice closes the browser without leaving the page The lock is released when the page closes. If that release is lost, it expires 120 s after Alice's last renewal and Bob's page can take it —
6 Alice leaves the tab open and goes to lunch The open tab keeps renewing the lock: it never expires by itself. Bob must ask Alice or press Take over —
7 Bob opens a different object on the same device Nothing: locks are per object Bob's save
8 Bob opens the same object name on another device Nothing: locks are per device Bob's save

Case by case: a row of an object (sub-object)#

A row of a table (a back-end server of a pool, a content-routing rule of a policy, a VIP of a virtual server, a member of an IP list) belongs to its object. The object's lock covers all of its rows.

# Case Result
9 Alice has the policy open; Bob edits one of its rows Refused like case 2. The message names the object, not the row
10 Alice edits row 1 and Bob edits row 2 of the same object The second person is refused. Two people cannot edit different rows of the same object at the same time
11 Bob adds a row to the object Alice has open, from a FortiWeb editor Refused (the editor checks the object's lock before any row write)
12 Bob adds a row of an inline table on a FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator or FortiAnalyzer page Refused: that row is written as part of the object, so it is a change to the object
13 Bob adds a FortiADC child-table row (a row that is its own object, …_child_…) Allowed: adding overwrites nothing
14 A job or script adds a row (POST) Allowed: adding overwrites nothing
15 A job changes or deletes a row (PUT/DELETE with sub_mkey) Refused like case 16

Case by case: a person and a job#

# Case Result
16 Mass Deploy, a Process, Policy Clone, a script, a scheduled action, the certificate or DNS-decommission jobs, or a FortiADC writer changes or deletes an object someone else has open Refused before it reaches the device. The job step shows PUT /api/v2.0/cmdb/<collection> · 409 and its error HTTP 409 — errcode edit-lock: "" is being edited by . Take over the edit lock first; nothing was sent to the device. The Audit Log records config.write.edit_locked with the method and the reason
17 The job was started by the person who holds the lock Allowed: your own lock never blocks your own job
18 The job has nobody behind it (a schedule with no owner, the scheduler itself) Refused by any lock: an unattended run never writes over an open edit
19 A job creates a new object or adds a row Allowed
20 An HTTP Observatory fix plan touches an object someone has open The whole plan is refused before its first write: is being edited by ; nothing was sent to the device.
21 Sentinel's automated response while someone has its objects open Adding an address to the satom-sentinel-block list (POST) still works. Removing an address from it (DELETE), and binding the list to a policy or Web Protection Profile (PUT), are refused while someone has that list, policy or profile open
22 A REST API (v1) or API Explorer call Treated as the signed-in user of the call. A lock held by that same user, in any tab, does not block it

Case by case: one person, two tabs#

A lock belongs to the page load that took it, not to the user.

# Case Result
23 You open the same object in a second tab or window Banner 🔒 You have this open in another tab or window. Saving here is blocked so the two do not overwrite each other. Save answers You have this object open in another tab or window. Take over the lock here first. A save sent anyway is refused with "" is being edited by you, in another tab or window. …
24 You press Take over in the second tab The second tab holds the lock; the first one shows Your edit lock was lost
25 You close the second tab The first tab keeps its lock (a tab can only release its own)
26 You reload the tab that holds the lock The reloaded page is a new page load. The old lock is released when the page unloads; if that release is lost, the reloaded page shows "another tab" for up to 120 s. Press Take over
27 You duplicate the tab The copy is a new page load and is treated as another tab

Case by case: the value changed since your page loaded#

The stale-value check runs on every save from an editor, whether or not anybody holds a lock. Your page sends, for each field you changed, the value the field had when the page loaded. SATOM reads the object from the device just before writing and compares.

# You loaded Device now You send Result
28 comment = a a c Saved: nobody changed it
29 comment = a b (someone saved it after your page loaded) c Refused, nothing sent. A table shows Field · You loaded · Device now · Yours = comment · a · b · c
30 comment = a b b Saved: the same change made twice is not a conflict
31 comment = a, port = 80 comment = b, port = 80 only port = 81 Saved. Only the fields you changed are sent, so comment keeps b
32 comment = a b, changed on the FortiWeb GUI or CLI directly c Refused, as in case 29: the check reads the device, not SATOM's copy
33 comment = a b, changed by a job c Refused, as in case 29
34 comment = a changed between your preview and Apply c The preview passed; Apply is refused, as in case 29

When a save is refused as stale, you choose:

  • Reload (object editor) / Cancel (Server Policy page and GUI dialogs). SATOM first refreshes its own copy of the object from the device, so the reloaded page shows the device's current values. This matters for the FortiWeb-layout dialogs, which draw from SATOM's copy: without the refresh the reload would show the old value and the next save would be refused again.
  • Overwrite with mine (object editor) / OK (Server Policy page and GUI dialogs). Your values are sent anyway. The Audit Log records config.update.overwrote with the object and the fields you replaced.

How values are compared#

  • Case and surrounding spaces are ignored (Enable = enable).
  • A number and its text are equal (80 = "80").
  • An empty field and a missing value are equal.

Fields that are never compared (they never block a save)#

Field Why
Secrets: any field whose name contains pass, secret, psk, private or token The device does not return them, or returns them encrypted
Values the device masks (******) No real value to compare
Tables and lists (a row list, a multi-value list) Compared row by row only when you edit a row
Counters the device keeps itself (sz_…) They change without anyone editing
Fields the device's read does not return, for example a field only the CLI serves ("Not in GUI, but in CLI") Nothing to compare with
Fields you did not change They are not sent, so they cannot overwrite anything

If the device does not answer the read, the check is skipped and the write itself reports what is wrong.

What each surface shows#

Surface Lock Stale value
Object editor (full page, inline, slide-over) Banner with Take over; Save blocked Table Field · You loaded · Device now · Yours with Reload and Overwrite with mine
Server Policy page One lock per object the page writes (the policy, its server pool, its virtual server); a banner for each one somebody else holds; each section is blocked only by its own object's lock A confirmation box listing the fields: OK overwrites, Cancel reloads
GUI-layout dialogs (FortiWeb, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer) Banner with Take over when editing an existing object or row; none on Create New Same confirmation box
Jobs, Processes, scripts, scheduled actions No banner: the step fails with the lock message Not applicable (jobs do not load a form)

What is not covered#

Case Why
Creating or cloning an object, and adding a row from a job Adding overwrites nothing; a name clash is refused by the device itself
Objects without a name (device-wide settings forms) A lock needs a name. The stale-value check still applies to them in the editors
FortiWeb settings forms saved through FortiWeb's own GUI API (log settings, admin settings) Neither the lock nor the stale-value check applies
A change made directly on the device while your page is open It cannot be prevented, only detected: your save is refused (case 32)
Architecture drawings and Wiki articles They have their own check: a save over a newer version is refused ( saved this drawing meanwhile). They do not take an edit lock

Audit Log and change history#

Event Action Detail
A write refused by a lock (job, script, API, other product's dialog) config.write.edit_locked PUT "<name>" is being edited by <user>. … and the endpoint as the target
An overwrite after a stale-value refusal config.update.overwrote mkey=<name> fields=<field>,<field>
An applied FortiWeb save refused as stale config.update with the error Also a change-history row with the error, nothing applied
Taking, renewing, releasing or taking over a lock none —

Advanced#

Advanced Lock keys, API fields and who counts as the writer
  • Lock key = <collection>:<object name> per device. FortiWeb: server-policy/policy:pol-shop. FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer: the page's collection, for example radiusclients:2. FortiADC: the entity, for example load_balance_pool:lb1. A row write is checked against every level above it (server-policy/policy/http-content-routing-list + pol-shop is covered by server-policy/policy:pol-shop), and a FortiADC child entity load_balance_pool_child_pool_member is covered by load_balance_pool.
  • Where it is enforced: the FortiWeb client refuses PUT/PATCH/DELETE on a cmdb path with ?mkey=; the FortiADC client refuses PUT/DELETE on /api/<entity> with mkey or pkey; every FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer GUI save is checked before its dry run. The editors check again with the page's token.
  • Who is writing, in this order: the signed-in user of the request; else the user who started the background job; else nobody (an unattended run).
  • Lock API: POST /api/locks/acquire|heartbeat|release|steal with appliance_id, resource_key and token (the page's token). An answer for a lock held by another page of the same user carries same_user: true. The token is never returned.
  • Save fields: lease_token (the page's token), expected ({field: value loaded}), overwrite: true. A stale refusal answers 409 with conflict ({field: {loaded, device, yours}}); an overwrite answers overwrote with the same shape. A caller that sends no lease_token is matched on the user; a caller that sends no expected gets no stale-value check.

Troubleshooting#

A job step fails with "errcode edit-lock"#

Possible causes — someone has the object (or the object the row belongs to) open in an editor.

Solution — check the Audit Log entry config.write.edit_locked for the name, let the person finish or take over the lock, then run the job again.

My save keeps being refused as stale after Reload#

Possible causes — the device itself keeps changing the field (a value the firmware recomputes), or the page reloaded from a copy that could not be refreshed because the device did not answer.

Solution — compare Device now across two attempts. If it changes on its own, use Overwrite with mine only if you mean to replace it; otherwise check the device's reachability first.
